title: Mild UV–X-Ray Slope Evolution Reduces Apparent High-Redshift Distance Compression in Unified-Flow Quasar Cosmography
content: A joint analysis of Pantheon+SH0ES Type~Ia supernovae and a 2421-object quasar UV--X-ray catalog examines whether mild redshift evolution in quasar standardization can reduce an apparent high-redshift transition in the Unified-Flow distance law. Four model classes combine single- or two-regime distance laws with a constant or minimally evolving UV--X-ray slope. With the slope held constant, the two-regime fit yields an extreme high-redshift exponent, $\beta_{\rm high}=14.3310$. Allowing $\gamma(z)=\gamma_0+\gamma_1\ln(1+z)$ shifts the best fit to $\beta_{\rm high}=0.9528$, with $\Delta\gamma\simeq-0.016$ between $z=0$ and $z=7$. A single-regime model with slope evolution also reduces the high-redshift residual drift toward zero. Low-redshift calibration and the reported held-out quasar scores show the same reduction in the incremental benefit of a distance-law step. Likelihood differences and conventional AIC/BIC scores provide comparative diagnostics; no Wilks-based significance is assigned to the step tests because the transition redshift is unidentified under the no-step null. The central result is the sensitivity of the extreme best-fit distance-law exponent to small changes in quasar standardization. Substantial high-redshift distance compression remains in the evolving-slope fit. Quantitative, model-conditional predictions are stated for independent quasar catalogs and high-redshift distance indicators.
